comment: ORCHID literature values, Version 1, machine-extracted. Evidence class: experimental. ORCHID observation ids (orchid-literature `id`, one per value, in value order): ORC-2CKRUYB3DW.6cdbc4

orchid_uncertainty.weight_rule: weight = default_sigma / this observation's sigma_effective_used; unequal-uncertainty groups are split into single-observation datasets, retaining their common source provenance
orchid_uncertainty.sigma_rule: sigma_effective = max(sqrt(max(printed, reading, method)^2 + composition^2 + conversion^2), scatter) (literature release `uncertainty_budget`; components kept per value in `budget`)

printed.interval: ±x printed; coverage not stated, taken as 1 sigma

orchid_weight_floor.superseded: superseded on 2026-10-24 (PI decision): the dataset weight now follows sigma_effective of the published uncertainty budget (method-class floors calibrated from ORCHID, never below ESPEI's experimental default) by default, so no opt-in is needed; this block keeps the former optional suggestion (sigma floor = ESPEI's default) for comparison only
orchid_weight_floor.rule: former optional minimum-sigma policy (E6, superseded): sigma_eff = max(sigma, sigma_floor) with sigma_floor = ESPEI's experimental default for the property (500 J/mol for enthalpies and for the chemical potential of activities, 0.2 J/mol/K for entropies and heat capacities); suggested_weight = min(weight, 1). The printed sigma is unchanged (orchid_uncertainty); use suggested_weight when printed sigmas are much smaller than the scatter between sources (e.g. formation enthalpies printed with +-80 J/mol-atom while other measurements differ by 1-2 kJ/mol-atom)

orchid_weighting.correlation_note: Shared source and method/calibration provenance are retained. Splitting does not establish statistical independence. No covariance is invented; the ESPEI likelihood used here does not model cross-observation covariance.
